      • editApplicationKvRecord

        public ResponseObject<ApplicationKvRecord> editApplicationKvRecord(java.lang.String applicationIdentifier,
                                                                   java.lang.String key,
                                                                   java.util.List<PatchRequest> request)
                                                            throws HttpException,
                                                                   HttpBadRequestException
        Requires the application's own access token - personal access tokens are not supported. Supported paths: /value, /ttl. To remove the TTL send null for /ttl using ApplicationKvRecordPatchRequest (a plain PatchRequest omits null values).

        Use ApplicationKvRecordPatchRequest for records that may be secret: its toString() masks every value except the /ttl one, while a plain PatchRequest prints the value as is.

        Note: the client omits null-valued entries inside maps when serializing the request, e.g. {"a": null, "b": 1} is sent as {"b": 1}; null elements inside lists are kept.

        Parameters:
        applicationIdentifier - identifier of the application
        key - key of the record (reserved characters are URL-encoded by the client)
        request - request object
        Returns:
        updated application KV record
        Throws:
        HttpException
        HttpBadRequestException
        See Also:
        • API Documentation
        • Enterprise API Documentation
